title: Content security gate for skill assimilation (scan + reviewer + mandatory sign-off)
description: Human policy decision from the TASK-120 UAT: license is NOT a safety assurance, and a self-declared frontmatter license is forgeable. Every third-party skill must pass a content security review, independent of license, before adoption, and NOTHING adopts without explicit human sign-off. Builds on TASK-120's assimilate workflow (which after its fix returns pending_approval and writes only on approve). This ticket adds the safety layers that populate the approval package. Scope: (1) an automated risky-pattern scan module over the fetched skill content; (2) a security-reviewer subagent step, orchestrator-driven, that reads the actual content INCLUDING the skill's instructions (prompt-injection is the key skill-specific risk a code scanner cannot catch) and returns a safe/suspicious verdict with reasoning; (3) the orchestrated flow that assembles license + provenance + scan findings + reviewer verdict and requires explicit human approval to adopt. Trust model: license/scan/reviewer are all decision-support; the human is the gate. Update docs/design/addon-packs.md §4 (trust boundary) and §7 (assimilation) to enshrine 'no auto-adopt; content review + sign-off always'.
acceptance_criteria: A skill content pattern-scan module (e.g. src/skill-scan.js) returns structured findings for risky patterns: shell/exec invocation, network/URL fetch, env/credential/filesystem access outside the skill dir, and base64/obfuscated/binary blobs; each finding carries a category, a location, and a severity.

The scan is exercised by tests over fixtures: a benign doc-only skill yields no findings; a skill containing (e.g.) a curl|sh, an env-var exfil, and a base64 blob yields the corresponding categorized findings.

The assimilation flow assembles an approval package {license verdict, provenance (origin/pin/integrity), scan findings, security-reviewer verdict} and adopts ONLY on explicit human approval; there is NO code path that writes an assimilated skill or lock entry without an explicit approve (verified by test).

A security-reviewer step reads the fetched skill content including its instruction text and returns a safe|suspicious verdict with reasoning; a suspicious verdict blocks adoption pending an explicit human override.

End-to-end (UAT): assimilating a real skill runs fetch -> license -> scan -> reviewer -> presented package -> human sign-off, and nothing is written until the human approves; a declined package leaves the tree and lock untouched.

docs/design/addon-packs.md §4 and §7 are updated to state: license is decision-support only, a content security review is mandatory and license-independent, and no third-party skill auto-adopts without human sign-off.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
Closed on a clean Reviewer APPROVE (fresh-context, full depth). Review depth = FULL; rubric inputs: diff touches the security surface (new src/skill-scan.js + src/assimilate.js content-security gate) and core tdd-tier logic (mandatory-FULL surfaces), changed-lines well over 150. tdd two-commit discipline verified: test commits (cc28e39, 64083e6) strictly precede impl (7130b1d) + docs (fd9226c); red-run independently reproduced at the impl parent (module genuinely absent). All 6 ACs satisfied; the no-write-without-approve (AC3) and suspicious-blocks-without-override (AC4) invariants were confirmed in the code, not just tests, with non-vacuous byte-untouched sensors. No scan/reviewer leakage into the persisted lock/provenance. Gate green: 767 fast passed/2 skipped, assimilate+skill-scan e2e 33 passed; dist-parity clean; no TASK-120 regression.

Post-approval hardening: the review's LOW finding (securityOverride truthiness) was fixed in dc393d3 — gate now requires strict boolean true (securityOverride !== true), with a red-green regression test asserting a truthy non-boolean 'no' still yields blocked_security with tree+lock untouched. Accepted without a second full-reviewer spawn: it is a verbatim application of the gating review's own recommendation on a one-line change, backed by a proven non-vacuous regression test.

Knowledge capture (TASK-105): not triggered — clean first-pass APPROVE, no HIGH finding and no REQUEST-CHANGES loop.

Security-reviewer runtime seam: src/assimilate.js stays LLM/network-free by design. The safe|suspicious verdict is an INJECTED input ({verdict, reasoning}) + securityOverride; the Orchestrator spawns the real security-reviewer subagent on fetched content (incl. instruction text, for prompt-injection) at assimilate time and passes the verdict back. This is what the design pack's live-adoption path (Diseño Poderoso) now depends on.

Unrelated fix landed alongside (not linked to this ticket): 7bda594 chore bumps tests/publish-config.spec.js EXPECTED_VERSION 0.11.0 -> 0.12.0 to match plugin.json, restoring a green fast tier (was pre-existing-red on main from the v0.12.0 bump in 531cdf4).
